title: Plant Tissue Fixation Protocol
author: Alex Rajewski
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.rw8d7hw
materials: Many different fixative recipes are possible. This is the most common. It can be made with either 100% ethanol or (more cheaply) 95% ethanol. This recipe can be scaled up or down proportionally. Prepared fixative can be store for many months, and can even be reused.

steps.title: Prepare samples with FAA
steps.instruction: Fill each sample tube with approximately 2 volumes of FAA relative to the tissue size (e.g., 2 mL of FAA for ~1cm³ of tissue).

substeps.instruction: Use fresh FAA for in situ fixation; previously used FAA may be used otherwise.

steps.title: Vacuum infiltrate samples
steps.instruction: Place tubes in the vacuum chamber and infiltrate the tissues.

substeps.instruction: Seal the chamber by turning the bleeder valve straight and turning off the pump.
Allow samples to infiltrate under vacuum for at least 1 hour (tissues larger than 1cm³ may require more time).

steps.title: Release vacuum and seal tubes
steps.instruction: Slowly dissipate the vacuum and secure the samples.

substeps.instruction: Open the bleeder valve slowly over 1-2 minutes to avoid damaging tissues.
Once the chamber is at equilibrium, open the chamber and close all tubes.

steps.title: Fix tissues overnight
steps.instruction: Allow samples to soak in the fixative overnight in a rack located within a fume hood.

steps.title: Transfer samples to ethanol
steps.instruction: Replace the fixative with a preservation solution.

substeps.instruction: Decant used fixative into a hazardous waste container.
Replace fixative with a solution of 50% ethanol.

steps.title: Perform secondary vacuum infiltration
steps.instruction: Place the ethanol-preserved samples back into a vacuum chamber in the fume hood.

substeps.instruction: Seal the chamber and pull a vacuum to approximately -0.08 mPa.
Monitor samples for small bubbles (normal); if fixative bubbles rapidly like boiling, slow down the vacuum or release some vacuum to stop the boiling.
